source.title: SafeEraser: Enhancing Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models through Multimodal Machine Unlearning
source.authors: Jun-Kai Chen; Zhi-Jie Deng; Ke-Ning Zheng; Yibo Yan; Shu-Liang Liu; Peijun Wu; Pei-Jie Jiang; Jia Liu; Xu-Ming Hu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether attacks can recover targeted harmful responses after multimodal unlearning, using behavioral ASR rather than the original studies’ unlearning settings.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates post-unlearning prompt-based attacks (role-play, ten-shot prompting, poetry) and an image-based OCR-style attack. It also reports ordinary unlearning efficacy and utility, but the rows below focus on the reported attack outcomes and the text’s aggregate efficacy statement. The ten-shot condition supplies in-context examples; it is not fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: New setting (multimodal LLaVA-v1.5 safety unlearning on SafeEraser). It measures harmful-response ASR after GA/GD/KL/PO unlearning, utility on seven benchmarks, and prompt- and image-based attacks on the unlearned models. These bear on A, E and, for the authors' PD Loss, F.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misplaced emphasis. The main conclusion is that existing MU methods forget harmful knowledge (near-zero ASR, good generality) but suffer over-forgetting and utility loss. PD Loss cuts SARR by 79.5% while preserving forget quality and utility. Lower ASR under jailbreaks with PD is a secondary finding.
record.recipe_differences: Applies GA, GD, KL, and preference optimization to multimodal safety unlearning on SafeEraser; evaluates multimodal prompt and image attacks rather than quantization, activation editing, or recovery fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type and use of PD Loss affect ASR; the reported attack study is on LLaVA-v1.5-7B.

fits_no_version.finding: After unlearning, all GA/GD/KL/PO models refuse about 100% of harmless images paired with forget-set prompts (SARR). The authors read this as the model forgetting the prompts rather than the knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning overgeneralises to the forget-set prompt template (over-forgetting) rather than selectively removing the harmful knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Attack results are reported only for LLaVA-v1.5-7B and are averaged over six harmful categories. Table 3 does not give a vanilla-model result under the same attack conditions, and the reported attack ASRs are not accompanied by uncertainty estimates. The extracted rows do not quantify retained general ability.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: Table 1 and Appendix Tables 7–13 contain further efficacy and model-utility results for individual methods, models, categories, and benchmarks. The rows above retain the aggregate efficacy statement relevant to A and the attack outcomes relevant to A, E, and F.

untested.parts: Attack resistance tested only on LLaVA-v1.5-7B with GD and KL; not on GA, PO or 13B.
No activation-direction ablation or internal analysis.
Other languages and optimized jailbreaks not tested; only role-play, ten-shot in-context and poetry rephrasing; 7B only, GD and KL only.
PD Loss not tested against fine-tuning, activation ablation or quantization; it was designed against over-forgetting, not attack robustness.

missing.what: Specificity on seven benchmarks per method; GA/GD/KL collapse general ability (e.g., 7B GD SQA 0.0, MMB-en 0.0)
SARR of 98.6–100% for all base methods (over-forgetting)
Per-category efficacy: Hate Speech 7B GD 16.3, KL 16.2, KL+PD 32.6 ASR vs vanilla 44.5
Generality ASR on held-out forget-test set (0.0–2.8 for 7B)

record.verdict_notes: The attack table has no vanilla-under-attack baseline and no uncertainty, so the differences between PD and the base methods (a few points) cannot be checked for noise. The ASR judge is GPT-4o. E rows are marked absent rather than partial because the rise over the unlearned model is at most 2.2 points against a 64% original rate. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because this is a multimodal setting.

versions.untested_parts: The extracted rows cover harmful-response ASR and attack resistance, but do not quantify retained general ability. The study does report utility metrics, which are not included here.
No fine-tuning attack on a small unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-access analysis is tested.
Tests role-play, ten-shot in-context examples, and poetry rephrasing, but not other languages or other prompting attacks.
Tests Prompt Decouple Loss against the reported prompt- and image-based attacks; does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization.

relation.reason: It reports attack-resistance results for unlearned models, so it tests A and E. F is tested only for the authors' own PD.

tranche.reason: New setting (multimodal safety unlearning on LLaVA) with attack results on the claim. The attacks are the paper's own, not the original's method.

source_check.notes: Attack results (Table 3) cover only 7B GD/KL with and without PD; no 13B, GA or PO attacks. The attack query split is not stated, and ASR is judged by GPT-4o. The KL+PD image row (0.2 vs KL 3.7) is the unlisted 18th row. Not in any row: PD weakens KL's forgetting (7B efficacy 5.5 vs 2.7; Hate Speech 32.6 vs KL 16.2, vanilla 44.5). Sec 4.2 argues, without testing, that over-forgetting means prompts are forgotten rather than knowledge.

statements.correction: Table 1 efficacy ASR: 7B vanilla 64.1, GA/GD/KL/PO 0.0-2.7, KL+PD 5.5. 13B vanilla 62.3, 0.0-1.2 without PD. Table 3 (7B GD/KL): 3.3-4.9.
statements.problem: The SafeEraser part is right: 64.1/62.3 vanilla, near-0 efficacy, and 7B GD/KL attack ASR 3.3-4.9. It omits that GA/GD/KL lose general ability (Table 7), that KL+PD efficacy is 5.5, and that Hate Speech 7B GD/KL efficacy stays about 16. Attacks were run only on 7B GD/KL (with and without PD).

statements.correction: Table 3: GD RA 3.5, TPA 3.4, PA 4.4; KL RA 4.9, TPA 3.8, PA 4.2. Table 1: GD/KL 7B efficacy 2.7. TPA uses 10 benign QA pairs from other domains.
statements.problem: Numbers are right: on 7B GD/KL, role-play, ten-shot and poetry ASR is 3.4-4.9, against 2.7 unlearned and 64.1 vanilla. The ten-shot examples are benign QA from other domains, not the forgotten facts. No vanilla-under-attack baseline is given, and the attack split is not stated.

statements.correction: SafeEraser, LLaVA-v1.5-7B, Table 3: GD+PD ASR is RA 0.0, TPA 0.1, PA 0.5, image 0.0, vs GD 3.5, 3.4, 4.4, 3.3. Vanilla efficacy ASR is 64.1. PD is the authors' own method. ACL 2025, code available, no uncertainty reported; base ASR already near floor.
statements.problem: Cites r4 (GD+PD role-play ASR 0.0, which does support F) but states no SafeEraser result. Its 'why' line ('All four are preprints') leaves out this ACL study. No numbers are given for this study.

statements.correction: Table 3 (LLaVA-v1.5-7B): KL+PD RA 1.7, TPA 2.1, PA 2.9, image 0.2, vs KL 4.9, 3.8, 4.2, 3.7. Table 1, no attack: KL+PD efficacy ASR 5.5, generality ASR 2.8; vanilla 64.1. No retrain reference, no uncertainty. These rows fit F support, not limits_scope.
statements.problem: Cites r12/r14/r16 as attacks weakening a counter-method. But KL+PD ASR under attack is no higher than KL+PD's own no-attack ASR, and there is no retrain reference. LLaVA is not among the '3B-8B Llama' conditions. No numbers are given for this study.
